purpose: Design-only information-dissemination frontier derived from literature review; no performance, ranking, tuning, holdout selection, promotion or live execution.

candidates.name: Public-information dissemination breadth
candidates.mechanism: At a fixed historical decision boundary, measure how many genuinely independent public information channels have disclosed the same event/state. The construct is dissemination breadth/salience, not content sentiment and not raw media volume.
candidates.event_clock: For each channel, earliest defensible public-observation timestamp from an immutable historical snapshot. Channel count is evaluated at the frozen decision boundary; later copies cannot retroactively increase historical breadth.
candidates.direction: two-sided outcome; no sign assumed ex ante
cheap_falsifiers: collapse all channels sharing the same upstream feed and verify the construct changes materially; otherwise discard as duplicate sourcing
future-row insertion test: later channel observations must not change the historical breadth state
timestamp substitution test: occurrence/action time must not substitute for first public observation
source-withdrawal/correction mutation must preserve the original historical prefix
channel permutation within calendar blocks must not create artificial event concentration
gates: immutable historical archive for every included channel
documented channel provenance and independence classes
non_overlap: Q206 is better treated as a Q204 cross-channel subcase
C31 concerns content persistence, not dissemination breadth
Q202 concerns information absence at a statutory boundary

synthesis_decisions.reason: Cross-channel arrival gap is a special case of public-information latency; retain only if channel independence is explicitly frozen.
Network diffusion remains a distinct mechanism, but historical graph freezing is the dominant evidence burden.
Science-to-patent translation is a provenance subcomponent of patent-publication/citation information rather than a separate first-class family.
The proposed rating-agency/company-channel pair is operationally weak and likely to introduce proprietary-provider dependence and channel non-independence.
Public-web literature supports studying information propagation, while the project can make the construct deterministic if channel provenance and snapshots are frozen.

evidence_basis: Kargarzadeh et al. (2026), arXiv:2608.14014: public news effects concentrate before/at publication; first reports and follow-up coverage should be separated; coverage itself is a baseline risk.
Jazbec et al. (2020), arXiv:2010.12002: public web news propagation to markets can be measured from historical Common Crawl archives.
Yu et al. (2026), arXiv:2606.29734: different information components of the same earnings event arrive at materially different speeds.
Ren et al. (2026), arXiv:2605.08726: information can diffuse across connected stocks through media, disclosure and investor channels; speed heterogeneity matters.
